extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent applicants/attorneys for citation guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners on how to cite references, prepare PTO-892 entries, handle applicant-submitted citations and corrections, and draft complete and clear Office actions including language for rejections and responses to applicant arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Related Art by Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP § 609 sets forth guidelines for applicants, their attorneys and agents who desire to submit prior art for consideration by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted citations will not in any way diminish the obligation of examiners to conduct independent prior art searches, or relieve examiners of citing other pertinent prior art of which they may be aware. Prior art submitted by applicant in the manner provided in MPEP § 609 will not be supplied with an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Related Information by Applicants (37 CFR 1.105 / MPEP §704.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for examiners to require applicants to submit information reasonably necessary for the Office to examine an application or treat a matter in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such requirement, and any information submitted in reply, will not diminish the examiner's obligation to conduct independent prior art searches. Information submitted in the manner provided in MPEP § 704.10 et seq. will not be supplied with an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Listing / Use of PTO-892
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing references for the first time, identifying data of the citation should be placed on form PTO-892 'Notice of References Cited' and a copy attached to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No distinction between references on which a claim is rejected and those formerly referred to as 'pertinent.' Pertinent features of recommended references which are not used as a basis for rejection should be pointed out briefly. See MPEP § 1302.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Cited in Subsequent Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant in an amendatory paper refers to a reference that is later relied upon by the examiner, the examiner shall cite the reference using form PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if applicant listed the reference on a form PTO/SB/08 that has been initialed by the examiner, separate PTO-892 citation may not be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Data When Citing U.S. Patent Documents (37 CFR 1.104(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. patent application publication or U.S. patent is cited by the examiner, include publication/patent number, publication/patent date, name of applicant/patentee, class, and subclass on PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are encouraged to cite kind codes printed on publications and patents. See MPEP § 901.04(a) for kind codes and § 901.04 for series details. Note special handling for X-Series patents and some 19th-century patents with two numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive Publications and SIRs Citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Defensive Publications and Statutory Invention Registrations should be cited under the 'U.S. Patent Documents' section on PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 711.06(a) and 901.06(a) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing Foreign Patents and Foreign Published Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing foreign patents include patent number, kind code, citation date, country, patentee name, and appropriate classification; use IPC subclass/group/subgroup where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If less than the entire disclosure is relied upon, include specific sheet/page numbers and total sheets/pages (except applicant-submitted citations). On 'Search Notes' FWF form and PTO-892, IPC subclass/group/subgroup shall be cited where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Publications and Non-Patent Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-patent documents should be cited under 'Non-Patent Documents' on PTO-892 and must include sufficient information to determine identity and facilitate location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For books: author, title, date (minimal). For periodicals: title, volume, issue, date, and pages. Call numbers guidance: STIC call numbers should not be cited; follow rules for copies located only in Technology Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Abbreviating Titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be abbreviated because abbreviations may not be sufficient to identify the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal bibliographic details may be used ONLY IF complete details are unknown or unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation Format for Withdrawn U.S. Patents and Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples provided for how to cite withdrawn U.S. patents and withdrawn U.S. patent application publications (include 'withdrawn' designation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formats: 'US 6,999,999, 10/2002, Brown et al., 403/155 (withdrawn).' and 'US 2002/0009999 A1, 7/2002, Jones et al., 403/155 (withdrawn)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Document Citation (WIPO ST.14 Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow WIPO ST.14 'Recommendation for the Inclusion of References Cited in Patent Documents' for electronic documents; format similar to paper documents with additional items where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include (A) medium type in [ ], (B) retrieval date in [retrieved on YYYY-MM-DD], (C) 'Retrieved from' source and address, (D) DOI or unique identifier if known, (E) ISBN/ISSN where necessary, (F) indicate format when multiple renderings exist, (G) paragraph/sentence/line numbers to locate cited material, (H) claim/figure/chemical/gene/program listing numbers, (I) specific headings when page/line not available, (J) specific passage words or pagination when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and Evidence of Electronic Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Office copies of electronic documents must be retained if the same document may not be available in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For internet/social media sources that cannot be downloaded, capture screenshots and provide an explanation of what the screenshots show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples for Electronic Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple concrete citation examples for documents retrieved from online databases, the Internet, CD-ROM, email, bulletin boards, social media (Twitter, YouTube), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow provided example formats (Examples 1–18) which show placement of [online], [retrieved on ...], 'Retrieved from:' and inclusion of accession numbers, DOIs, database names, URLs, and paragraph/paragraph identifiers when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Lengthy Non-Patent Document Citations on PTO-892
rubrics_metrics.description: When a citation is too lengthy to fit within the PTO-892 box (commonly URLs), continue the citation into the next box and clearly indicate continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The citation will be captured as one citation; explanatory wording such as '[item U continued]' will not be captured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect Citation of References — Correction Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When an error in citation is brought to the Office's attention, a correction letter and a correct copy of the reference is sent to applicant; if examiner discovers the error, applicant is notified and the period for reply is restarted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.81, 7.82, 7.82.01, and 7.83 as appropriate. Every correction MUST be reflected on a corrected or new PTO-892. Consult the SPE before restarting the period when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Action on Formal Matters (First Action Requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any form that lists informalities and additional formal requirements the examiner desires should be included in the first action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When formal requirements are made and allowable subject matter is indicated, the action should call attention to 37 CFR 1.111(b) and state that a complete reply must either comply with all formal requirements or traverse each requirement not complied with. Example form paragraph: 7.43.03 Allowable Subject Matter, Formal Requirements Outstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language To Be Used in Rejecting Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim is refused for any reason relating to the merits it should be 'rejected' and the ground of rejection fully and clearly stated; the word 'reject' must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate the statutory basis for any ground of rejection by express reference to a section of 35 U.S.C. in the opening sentence of each ground. Do not group claims in a common rejection unless equally applicable to all. The burden is on the Office to establish any prima facie case of unpatentability; the reasoning behind any rejection must be clearly articulated. In the first Office action on the merits, identify claims judged allowable and/or suggest amendments to make rejected claims allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note All Outstanding Requirements in Every Letter
rubrics_metrics.description: In taking up an amended application for action the examiner should note in every letter all requirements outstanding against the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every point in the prior action still applicable must be repeated or referred to, to prevent implied waiver. Include requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105 and MPEP §704.10 but determine whether satisfied by a negative reply under 37 CFR 1.105(a)(3). As soon as allowable subject matter is found, require correction of all informalities then present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer All Material Traversed (Responding to Applicant Arguments)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner must provide clear explanations of all actions taken during prosecution; answer the substance of applicant's arguments when they are traversed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid personal remarks or statements implying lack of professional judgment. If applicant traverses a rejection and the examiner repeats it, note and answer applicant's arguments. If arguments are persuasive and prior rejection is withdrawn, provide reasons in the next Office communication and refer specifically to applicant's pages/lines forming the basis (use form paragraphs such as 7.37–7.38, 7.38.01, 7.38.02). If withdrawal results in allowance, include reasons (see MPEP §1302.14). Use appropriate form paragraphs when arguments are persuasive, moot, or not persuasive; ensure the examiner addresses all arguments not already responded to in the statement of the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answering Asserted Advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant argues that cited prior art does not teach or inherently yield asserted advantages, the examiner should state reasons if the asserted advantages are not sufficient to overcome rejections of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the reasons in the record, preferably in the action following the assertion, so the applicant and PTAB will know the advantages were considered. See In re Herrmann and In re Soni for case law illustrating the importance of answering asserted advantages. Form paragraphs 7.37–7.37.13 (arguments not persuasive) and 7.38–7.38.02 (arguments persuasive or moot) may be used where appropriate.
